answer: Resist sybils with proof-of-space-time: each identity must prove it holds a distinct data replica across a whole epoch, answering spot challenges at random times. A walnut-sized allocation proves nothing alone; only a sustained signal of correct answers proves it stayed stored. Clones sharing one disk cannot answer simultaneous challenges for different replicas, so their weight collapses to one. An attacker minting ten thousand fakes must provision ten thousand disks, paying storage and power per fake, while an honest agent stores one replica — the kernel of its standing — cheaply.
